actions.heading: What to do first, in order
paragraphs: First, have the cloud administrator grant object read on {F104} refused buckets and decide on restoring {F105} archive buckets; this opens {F102} files to reading. Alongside it, reconcile the {F033} unlistable buckets with the provider so later cost decisions rest on a sound inventory.

Second, collect storage class and read demand for the {F036} TiB of cold data and reprice at actual tariffs, since {F019} USD is only a legacy ceiling. Hash-confirm {F034} TiB of duplicate candidates and fingerprint the file shares before any copy is removed.
Third, prepare the pilot products with de-identification or aggregation, and finish sampling and the {F075} unread transcripts. Database reclaim is only {F005} GiB, so it should not lead.

chapter1.heading: Where the bytes sit
paragraphs: The estate totals {F050} TiB, made up of {F030} TiB in the object store, {F040} TiB in file shares and {F052} TiB in databases. These are bytes listed or measured, not content read.
For the owner, storage cost and product raw material both sit in the buckets and shares, while the databases matter mainly for condition and personal-data preparation.

chapter10.heading: What the executive is asked to decide
paragraphs: The decisions table gives each request with its exact source, rule, responsible role and expected benefit. Cost decisions rest on {F036} TiB of cold bytes and {F034} TiB of duplicate candidates, both needing verification first.

Inventory decisions rest on {F033} unlistable buckets, distinct from the read refusals and restore needs. Corpus preparation rests on {F060} staged audio hours. {F019} USD a month is a legacy scenario, not a budget or a realised saving. Nothing here has been executed.

chapter11.heading: What remains unmeasured
paragraphs: Only {F003} of {F002} tables were measured, one database connection awaits a read grant, and {F033} object-store buckets cannot be listed. File shares of {F040} TiB and {F041} files lack content fingerprints, so duplication is unmeasured. {F075} transcripts are unread and script languages are station metadata.

Each gap has a closing step: a complete-pass census, inventory reconciliation, a fingerprinting pass and a text-model pass. The authoring table discloses the models that wrote this pack; it does not establish independent accuracy or census completeness.

chapter2.heading: What the review lists show
paragraphs: The tables beside this chapter name every bucket, table and share under review, with what was measured and where each is proposed to go. {F036} TiB of the object store has not been written for over a year, across {F037} buckets, and {F034} TiB are duplicate candidates matched on size and name.

Candidates are not confirmed copies, and file-share duplication is not measured. {F033} of {F032} buckets returned errors when listed and need reconciling with the provider. All destinations are proposals; nothing has been moved or deleted.

chapter4.heading: What state the database rows are in
paragraphs: Exact duplicates are {F007} of rows, so duplicate removal alone achieves little. The larger problems are completeness and damage: {F009} of rows have empty required-looking fields and {F008} are degraded. The required-looking flag is a heuristic, so the owner should decide which fields truly must be filled.

{F010} of {F011} sampled rows carry personal-data markers. This is a measured condition, not a proven breach and not a rights question; the owner's declaration settles rights. De-identification or aggregation is a preparation step for any product. {F012} of database bytes have not been written for over a year.

chapter5.heading: Staged audio: duration, speech and quality
paragraphs: The staged corpus holds {F060} recorded hours in {F068} language folders. Speech is {K010} of that, an estimated {F061} hours, with {F062} hours of music, and {F074} files are mostly music. Music filtering is therefore the first preparation step for any speech set.

Both GPUs read {F063} files in {F067} GPU-hours. The tables beside this chapter give files, hours, agreement and quality signals by folder. Noise and intelligibility were not scored, and every reading is a model reading, not a human label.

chapter6.heading: Written text the estate holds
paragraphs: The news archive holds {F080} live scripts and {F084} characters, but only on {F082} calendar dates across {F083} days. Revisions are {F085} of rows, {F086} distinct texts remain and {F087} rows are marked deleted, so revisions must be resolved before any corpus use.

The text model read {F070} transcripts and {F071} of passages agree with the folder language; {F075} transcripts were not reached. The workbench registers {F090} recordings, {F091} hours and {F092} segments in {F094} languages. It is a separate inventory that may overlap the staged corpus, so the two are never added.

chapter7.heading: What can be read, and what cannot
paragraphs: Of listed object-store media files, {F101} sit in readable buckets and {F102}, {F103} TiB, sit in buckets the key cannot read, so {F113} are beyond reach today. {F104} buckets refuse object reads and {F105} need a restore first. Their content is counted, never estimated.

In the readable scope, hours are estimated at {F106}, with {F107} speech and {F108} music; speech is {K020} of the header total. The estimators need not add to it. Sampling is unfinished, so granting access and completing the high-volume folders will improve this baseline most.

chapter8.heading: Storage class, reading cost and file-share progress
paragraphs: Storage class is known only for a subset of buckets. In that subset {F114} of bytes are already archive class, which leaves no Standard-to-Archive saving there. This does not describe the whole object store, and unknown classes are not assumed either way.

Reading the content so far has cost an estimated {F111} USD of egress at an assumed tariff, with archive retrieval fees unpriced. File shares measured so far hold {F121} hours, {F122} of them speech, from {F123} files read; {F124} shares are still listing or probing and are not counted.

chapter9.heading: Which products to prepare first
paragraphs: {F018} product candidates were scored on readiness. Reference and master data, content catalogue and channel engagement are each graded C, and are proposed as the first pilots because their preparation is bounded. Others carry heavier conditions such as stale supporting tables or lower grades, and should follow.

Every pilot needs de-identification or aggregation, because personal-data markers are widespread in the supporting tables. That is preparation, not a rights question. The order is a recommendation to test with buyers, not a measured commercial ranking, and audio or text extensions would be model-read and uncertified.

compare.heading: Three options, each conditional
paragraphs: Archiving buckets idle for over a year addresses {O1.reclaimable_gib} GiB at up to {O1.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month. Reconciling duplicate objects addresses {O2.reclaimable_gib} GiB at up to {O2.monthly_saving_usd} USD, and moving old tables to cold storage addresses {O3.reclaimable_gib} GiB at up to {O3.monthly_saving_usd} USD.

All three are upper bounds at reference list prices. The legacy scenario of {F019} USD assumes full Standard price while storage classes are only partly measured, and bytes already in archive class have nothing left to save. Retrieval and restore fees are not priced, duplicates are unconfirmed, and options may overlap, so the figures should not be added.
Validate storage class and read demand before the first move, and hash-confirm duplicates before the second. The third is small and worth doing only alongside other table work.

exhibit_S001.heading: Database bytes sit in very few databases
paragraphs: The largest databases hold {F016} GiB of the {F004} GiB, which is {K002}. Targeted remediation there has the most operational leverage.
This exhibit is about concentration only. Database size is not a quality score, and the databases are {K007} of the {F050} TiB estate.

exhibit_S002.heading: Row condition: separate signals, not one whole
paragraphs: The chart shows five condition measures side by side: exact duplicates at {F007}, degraded rows at {F008}, empty required-looking fields at {F009}, personal-data markers in sampled rows at {F010}, and bytes not written for over a year at {F012}. Empty fields are the commonest row signal and exact duplicates the smallest.
These measures overlap, use different populations and include estimates, so they cannot be summed or read as shares of one whole. They indicate preparation work, not a verdict on the data.

exhibit_S003.heading: Where the addressable bytes are
paragraphs: Of the {F021} GiB that all cost strategies reach, archiving buckets idle for over a year addresses {O1.reclaimable_gib} GiB and reconciling duplicate objects {O2.reclaimable_gib} GiB. Moving old database tables addresses only {O3.reclaimable_gib} GiB. The three largest strategies together address {F020} GiB.

Addressed is not removed. Strategies may overlap, last-write age says nothing about reads, and part of the cold data may already sit in archive class. The chart shows where validation effort belongs, not what will be saved.

exhibit_S004.heading: The estate is mostly object and file storage
paragraphs: The chart splits the estate by store. The object store and file shares together dwarf the databases, which are {K007} of the {F050} TiB. Cost effort therefore belongs in {F030} TiB of buckets and {F040} TiB of shares, not in database tables.
Size is neither value nor coverage. Bytes held say nothing about whether content has been read, is readable, or is wanted by a buyer. Later sections deal with each of those separately.

exhibit_S005.heading: One bucket dominates the object store
paragraphs: The largest bucket holds {F038} TiB, which is {K008} of the {F030} TiB object store. Any cost or access decision about it moves the estate picture more than any other single item.
A large bucket is not proof of idleness, readability or redundancy. Read demand was not measured, so the sensible step is to gather evidence on it first, then decide.

exhibit_S010.heading: Estimated speech by language folder
paragraphs: Staged audio totals {F060} recorded hours, of which an estimated {F061} are speech once {F062} hours of music are set aside. The chart splits speech hours by language folder; the largest folders are broadly comparable and two small folders hold very little.
These are model estimates from header duration and a music detector. They describe the staged corpus only, not every language in the estate, and are not certified speech assets.

exhibit_S011.heading: Agreement with the folder language varies
paragraphs: Across all folders, {F072} of judged windows agree with the folder language, but the chart shows the spread between folders is wide. At least one folder, with very little speech, shows no agreeing windows.

Agreement is a model reading on labelled windows, and the model declined to label {F066} of speech windows. Low-agreement folders should go first to human review; the figure is not verified language accuracy.

exhibit_S012.heading: News scripts by station
paragraphs: The archive holds {F080} live scripts from {F081} stations, and the chart shows counts differ markedly between stations. The scripts are counted and sized, not read.

The language shown for each station is its broadcast language from the estate's own table, not a reading of the script text. A count of scripts is also not a count of unique texts, since {F085} of rows revise an earlier script.

exhibit_S013.heading: Bulletin hours on scripted days
paragraphs: On the days a station has any script, the number of distinct bulletin hours varies widely between stations, as the chart shows. Some stations script most of the day and one scripts far fewer hours.
The archive is therefore useful but discontinuous. Bulletin hour slots are not recorded audio duration and do not show continuous broadcasting.

exhibit_S020.heading: Hours held in the readable buckets
paragraphs: The readable buckets hold an estimated {F106} hours, and the chart shows a few buckets carry most of them. {F110} files were header-probed and the rest extrapolated by each folder's seconds-per-byte.
These are header-derived estimates, not decoded hours, and some durations use bitrate estimates. Validation effort should follow scale, starting with the largest buckets.

exhibit_S021.heading: Estimated speech by language
paragraphs: Across the readable stores, Kiswahili and Gikuyu lead estimated speech hours, with the other languages shown behind them. The totals rest on {F109} files read in full and carry sampling intervals.

The intervals exclude classification error. Abstentions and unsupported languages are not redistributed, and unread or inaccessible content is excluded, so the chart is a guide to where to validate, not a language inventory.

risks.heading: What the evidence cannot yet say
paragraphs: Row-condition ratios rest on {F003} measured tables of {F002}, and personal-data markers on a sample. Content in {F102} unreadable files, {F103} TiB, has no hours, speech or language estimate until access is granted. Sampling intervals exclude model error, so human checks including abstentions are needed.

{F124} file shares are still listing or probing, and duplication across shares is unmeasured. No invoice baseline exists and retrieval and restore fees are unpriced, so net savings cannot be stated. Each gap has a named closing step in the coverage ledger.

cautions: The owner’s declaration settles ownership and use rights; disregard contradictory legacy recommendations for renewed rights clearance, while retaining technical access, privacy preparation and execution-approval requirements.

Preserve the supplied outline, exhibit data and evidence; several needs, must-cite entries and table references have unresolved aliases, so flag those bindings rather than inventing tokens, silently remapping them or treating missing references as verified.

Producer claims and the older expert narrative are contextual, not replacements for the supplied evidence facts and scope qualifications; do not carry forward conflicting totals, unsupported quality measures or guaranteed-savings language.
Use only evidence tokens for figures and retain their measured, estimated or inferred status; do not calculate replacement totals, intervals, rankings or financial projections.
No invoice-backed estate carrying-cost baseline is supplied; {F019} is a historic reference-price scenario and {F111} is estimated census egress expenditure, not monthly storage cost.
Apply {F114} only to the storage-class-observed subset; unknown classes remain unknown, and bytes already archived have no remaining Standard-to-Archive saving.

Access-state descriptions and duplicate-candidate methods vary across the supplied sources; preserve source-specific qualifications and request reconciliation rather than asserting a uniform error or fingerprint method.

blocking: draft.paper.sections.chapter9.paragraphs[0]: States that the other five candidates 'carry heavier conditions such as stale supporting tables or lower grades'. The evidence contradicts this for two of them: time-series forecasting and transaction analytics are both grade C with the same single PII-preparation condition as the three chosen pilots, and their readiness scores (57.6) exceed the content catalogue's (56.8).
